Content: The Great Nebula in the constellation Orion consists primarily of excited hydrogen gas. The electrons in the atoms of excited hydrogen have been raised to higher energy levels. When these atoms release energy, a frequent electron transition is from the excited `n=3` energy level to the `n=2` energy level, which gives the nebula `text(one)` of its characteristic colors.
